N-1.1-A.skill: recover the instantaneous rate as the limit of an average-rate expression, and evaluate that same expression at a fixed h for a longer interval.

N-1.1-B.skill: decide whether an instantaneous rate exists from one-sided average rates over shrinking intervals.

N-1.2-A.skill: evaluate a limit of a composite h(f(x)) by tracking the side from which the inner function approaches its limit.

N-1.2-B.skill: judge which limit statements, including infinite and one-sided limits, are written correctly.

N-1.3-A.skill: transform one-sided limits read from a graph through a reflection, shift, or scaling of the input, tracking which side is approached.

N-1.3-B.skill: count points where a limit exists but differs from the function value or the value is undefined, from a verbal description of a graph.

N-1.4-A.skill: estimate a limit from a two-sided table, then transform it algebraically while ignoring the defined value at the point.

N-1.4-B.skill: recognize that a table sampled at special inputs cannot establish a limit when the function oscillates.

N-1.5-A.skill: use a limit of a difference quotient to deduce lim f, then apply product laws.

N-1.5-B.skill: decide what algebraic limit laws guarantee when one limit is infinite, zero, or nonexistent, using the converse-style argument.

N-1.6-A.skill: choose a parameter so a radical difference quotient has a finite limit, then evaluate it with the conjugate.

N-1.6-B.skill: evaluate trigonometric quotients that need a half-angle identity and the sin u / u limit together.

N-1.7-A.skill: match each limit with an appropriate procedure and identify which one has the stated value.

N-1.7-B.skill: locate the first error in a student's worked limit and recognize why the step fails.

N-1.8-A.skill: bound a quotient containing a bounded oscillating term and squeeze at infinity.

N-1.8-B.skill: use a bound on |f| to squeeze a quotient f(x)/xⁿ, and recognize when the bound is too weak.
